description: nf-core/seqinspector samplesheet context JSON template, aligned to the pinned 1.1.0 nextflow_schema.json and assets/samplesheet.csv. QC-only pipeline: no genome reference required.

tools_bundle.help: named bundle of QC tools to run

tools.help: explicit comma-separated tool list; overrides tools_bundle when set

skip_tools.help: comma-separated tools to skip from the selected bundle

subsample_tools.help: tools that run on a subsample rather than the full FastQ

sample_size.help: reads to subsample for subsample_tools; 0 means no subsampling

continue_with_lint_fail.help: keep going when fq_lint flags a file (default true — a lint failure should not abort a QC survey)

kraken2_db.help: REQUIRED if kraken2 is in the tool set. No kraken2 database is provisioned on Luria — leave kraken2 out of the bundle unless a db path is supplied.

pipeline.name: nf-core/seqinspector
pipeline.core_rule: Columns are sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, rundir, tags. Only sample and fastq_1 must carry a value; fastq_2 is blank for single-end, and rundir/tags are optional.
pipeline.reference_requirement: NONE. --genome/--fasta are optional; with neither, the pipeline skips the BWAMEM2 alignment step and every tool that depends on the alignment. This is the intended mode here: the Luria refs tree carries only fasta+gtf and no bwamem2 index, so requesting alignment would force an expensive per-run index build.
pipeline.multi_run_behavior: Rows sharing a sample value are treated as multiple runs/lanes of the same sample.
pipeline.single_vs_paired_behavior: Paired-end when fastq_2 is populated; single-end when blank.

validation_rules: The file consumed by the pipeline must be comma-separated (CSV).
sample must be non-empty; spaces are converted to underscores by the pipeline.
fastq_1 must be a gzipped FASTQ path ending in .fastq.gz or .fq.gz.
fastq_2 must be blank for single-end libraries and populated for paired-end libraries; the header must exist either way.
tags is a colon-separated list of group labels; every distinct tag produces its own MultiQC report in addition to the global one.
Do NOT add kraken2 to the tool set without also setting kraken2_db — the run will fail with no database.
Do NOT pass --gtf: seqinspector's schema has no gtf parameter and nf-schema aborts the run on an unrecognised param.
notes: QC-only. Nothing here writes analysis results worth reingesting as A.* samples — the output is MultiQC reports for human review. Use it to triage a cohort before committing to a full pipeline, or to audit sequencing data already registered in NExtSEEK.

sources.notes: Samplesheet columns, optional-genome behaviour, default tool set.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/seqinspector input samplesheet.

sample.description: Custom sample name. Repeat across rows for multiple lanes/runs of the same library.
sample.validation_hints: Prefer the NExtSEEK D.SEQ UID so the QC report maps back to the sample record.

fastq_1.validation_hints: Absolute Luria path; taken from the sample's Link_PrimaryData / File_PrimaryData metadata.

fastq_2.required: required header, value optional for single-end
fastq_2.description: Full path to read 2 FASTQ for paired-end libraries.
fastq_2.validation_hints: Leave blank for single-end; keep the header.

rundir.description: Sequencing run folder, used by rundirparser to collect instrument metadata.
rundir.validation_hints: Populate only when the run directory is known and readable on Luria; a wrong path fails the rundirparser tool.

tags.description: Grouping labels. Each distinct tag yields its own MultiQC report alongside the global one.
tags.validation_hints: This is the column worth populating from NExtSEEK metadata — cohort, treatment, genotype or study give per-group QC reports for free. Use short slugs; avoid commas.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Construct an nf-core/seqinspector samplesheet from a resolved NExtSEEK D.SEQ cohort.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected when the user asks to QC, inspect, survey or triage sequencing data rather than analyse it.
report_writer_guidance.output_expectation: Emit a pipeline-ready CSV with header sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,rundir,tags.
population_priority: One row per D.SEQ leaf sample; use the sample's UID as the sample value.
Map R1/R2 FASTQ paths from the sample's primary-data metadata; leave fastq_2 blank for single-end.
Leave rundir blank unless the run directory is genuinely known.

Populate tags from the cohort-defining metadata the user asked about (treatment, genotype, study, cohort) so the run yields per-group MultiQC reports. This is the main reason to run this from NExtSEEK rather than by hand.
Do not set a genome; the QC tools that matter here need none.
final_checks: Every row has a non-empty sample and fastq_1.
No --gtf, and no genome unless the user explicitly asked for the alignment-dependent tools.
kraken2 is absent from the tool set unless a kraken2_db path was supplied.
